# SurrealDB Documentation

SurrealDB is a [multi-model database](https://surrealdb.com/features) that stores relational, document, graph, time-series, vector, full-text and key-value data in one place, queried through [SurrealQL](https://surrealdb.com/docs/reference/query-language). It runs embedded in an application, as a single node, or as a distributed cluster, and is also available as [SurrealDB Agent Memory](https://surrealdb.com/docs/agent-memory), a memory and knowledge layer for AI agents.

> Markdown for agents: every documentation page is also available as markdown. Append ".md" to any page path to fetch it directly, for example "https://surrealdb.com/docs/reference/query-language/statements/select.md". The same document is served on the page's own URL to a request sending an "Accept: text/markdown" header, with "Content-Type: text/markdown" and an "x-markdown-tokens" estimate. HTML stays the default for browsers. Links inside a markdown page already point at the ".md" variants, so following them keeps an agent in markdown. The complete documentation is also available as a single markdown document at "https://surrealdb.com/docs/llms-full.txt".

Working notes:

- SurrealQL is the native query language. [GraphQL](https://surrealdb.com/docs/learn/querying/graphql/overview), [HTTP](https://surrealdb.com/docs/reference/rest-api/http-protocol), [RPC](https://surrealdb.com/docs/reference/rest-api/rpc-protocol) and [CBOR](https://surrealdb.com/docs/reference/rest-api/cbor-protocol) are also available.
- Live queries push changes to subscribers rather than requiring polling.
- The same database serves documents, graphs, vectors and time series inside one ACID transaction, so joins across models do not need a second store.

## Learn

- [Security](https://surrealdb.com/docs/learn/security): Learn how to secure your SurrealDB deployment with authentication, authorization, and security best practices.
- [Users](https://surrealdb.com/docs/learn/security/authentication/authentication): There are multiple forms of authentication built into SurrealDB, supporting server-side and client-side authentication.
- [Introduction](https://surrealdb.com/docs/learn/security/authentication/overview): An overview of how authentication works in SurrealDB, covering system users, record users, sessions, and third-party token integration.
- [Summary](https://surrealdb.com/docs/learn/security/authentication/summary): This page summarizes some of the security features offered by SurrealDB as well as some security elements of its development process with the goal of providing a starting point to both new and experienced users who wish to know more about the security of SurrealDB.
- [Capabilities](https://surrealdb.com/docs/learn/security/authorization/capabilities): SurrealDB is secure by default and is suitable for all database use cases. It offers powerful features like scripting, functions or network access from within your SurrealQL queries.
- [Permissions & row-level security](https://surrealdb.com/docs/learn/security/authorization/permissions-and-row-level-security): How SurrealDB's PERMISSIONS clause on tables and fields controls create, select, update, and delete, including per-record and field-level rules using $auth.
- [Tokens & JWTs](https://surrealdb.com/docs/learn/security/authorization/tokens-and-jwts): How SurrealDB authenticates clients with JWTs, DEFINE ACCESS TYPE JWT, symmetric and asymmetric verification, claims as session variables, and RECORD access for database-managed sign-in.
- [Security best practices](https://surrealdb.com/docs/learn/security/best-practices/security-best-practices): This guide outlines some key security best practices for using SurrealDB 3.0. While SurrealDB offers powerful and flexible features to support you in meeting your desired security standards, the use that you make of those features will ultimately determine whether or not you meet them.
- [Troubleshooting](https://surrealdb.com/docs/learn/security/best-practices/troubleshooting): This page provides some troubleshooting advice to support users in addressing issues either caused by or involved in the usage of specific security features provided by SurrealDB.
- [Schema management](https://surrealdb.com/docs/learn/schema-management): How to shape data in SurrealDB: tables, fields, indexes, events, tenancy, and related patterns.
- [Closures](https://surrealdb.com/docs/learn/schema-management/computed-data/closures): Anonymous functions in SurrealQL, colloquially known as closures.
- [Computed fields](https://surrealdb.com/docs/learn/schema-management/computed-data/computed-fields): Fields that are derived on read with COMPUTED, traversing record links, and how they differ from VALUE and stored data.
- [Defining events](https://surrealdb.com/docs/learn/schema-management/events-and-triggers/defining-events): Running logic after creates, updates, and deletes with DEFINE EVENT.
- [Reactive patterns](https://surrealdb.com/docs/learn/schema-management/events-and-triggers/reactive-patterns): Choosing between synchronous and asynchronous events, LIVE SELECT subscriptions, and evolving reactive behaviour safely.
- [Buckets](https://surrealdb.com/docs/learn/schema-management/files/buckets): Defining file buckets: memory, disk, global backends, and permissions.
- [Working with files](https://surrealdb.com/docs/learn/schema-management/files/working-with-files): File pointers, buckets, and putting or getting bytes from SurrealDB.
- [Index types and strategies](https://surrealdb.com/docs/learn/schema-management/indexes/index-types-and-strategies): Choosing indexes for lookups, uniqueness, full-text, vectors, and counts.
- [Namespace & database architecture](https://surrealdb.com/docs/learn/schema-management/multi-tenancy/namespace-and-database-architecture): Layering namespaces and databases for isolation, security, and strict mode.
- [Sample industry schemas](https://surrealdb.com/docs/learn/schema-management/schema-design/sample-industry-schemas): Copy-paste starter schemas for energy, finance, retail, medical, and other domains.
- [Schema best practices](https://surrealdb.com/docs/learn/schema-management/schema-design/schema-best-practices): Best practices for creating schemas in SurrealDB.
- [Schema design](https://surrealdb.com/docs/learn/schema-management/schema-design/schema-design): What DEFINE does in SurrealDB and how to inspect what you have defined.
- [Schema evolution](https://surrealdb.com/docs/learn/schema-management/schema-design/schema-evolution): Changing schema over time with ALTER and related patterns.
- [Fields and validation](https://surrealdb.com/docs/learn/schema-management/tables-and-fields/fields-and-validation): Defining fields: types, defaults, VALUE, ASSERT, permissions, and references.
- [Record ID best practices](https://surrealdb.com/docs/learn/schema-management/tables-and-fields/record-id-best-practices): How best to make a decision on what kind of record ID format to use in your database.
- [Record IDs and addressing](https://surrealdb.com/docs/learn/schema-management/tables-and-fields/record-ids-and-addressing): How record IDs work, ranges, and practical choices for addressing data.
- [Tables](https://surrealdb.com/docs/learn/schema-management/tables-and-fields/tables): Declaring tables: schemaless vs schemafull, relations, views, changefeeds, and permissions.
- [Extensions](https://surrealdb.com/docs/learn/extensions): Extend SurrealDB with custom modules and WASM plugins through the Surrealism extension system.
- [Creating custom modules](https://surrealdb.com/docs/learn/extensions/guides/creating-custom-modules): Step-by-step guide to scaffolding a Surrealism module, exposing functions with attributes, compiling and loading into SurrealDB.
- [Module architecture](https://surrealdb.com/docs/learn/extensions/guides/module-architecture): How Surrealism modules are packaged, sandboxed, and invoked by SurrealDB, including exports metadata, runtime limits, and load strategy.
- [Surrealism attribute reference](https://surrealdb.com/docs/learn/extensions/guides/surrealism-attribute-reference): Reference for the #[surrealism] attribute options, including writeable functions, comments, init hooks, and namespaced exports.
- [Using WASM plugins](https://surrealdb.com/docs/learn/extensions/guides/using-wasm-plugins): How to load a pre-built Surrealism module archive into SurrealDB, register it, inspect exports, and call functions from SurrealQL.
- [Further examples](https://surrealdb.com/docs/learn/extensions/plugins/further-examples): Further examples of Surrealism attributes, namespaced exports, and CLI commands
- [Surrealism plugins](https://surrealdb.com/docs/learn/extensions/plugins/overview): Surrealism is a plugin feature that allows users to compile Rust functions into modules that can be called from a SurrealDB instance.
- [Quick tutorial](https://surrealdb.com/docs/learn/extensions/plugins/quick-tutorial): A quick tutorial showing the steps involved in turning regular Rust code into SurrealDB-accessible WASM functions.
- [Data Models](https://surrealdb.com/docs/learn/data-models): Store and query document, graph, vector, time-series, and geospatial data with SurrealDB.
- [Architecture](https://surrealdb.com/docs/learn/data-models/architecture): How SurrealDB separates compute from storage, how every data model maps onto one storage engine, and how namespaces, databases and tables are structured.
- [Common patterns](https://surrealdb.com/docs/learn/data-models/document/common-patterns): Map document-database concepts to SurrealDB, compare SurrealQL with MongoDB-style operations, and find resources for CRUD and migration.
- [Nested objects and arrays](https://surrealdb.com/docs/learn/data-models/document/nested-objects-and-arrays): Store nested JSON-like structures in SurrealDB records, use SurrealQL examples with addresses and record links, and relate documents via fields such as article authors.
- [Document model](https://surrealdb.com/docs/learn/data-models/document/overview): Learn how to think in a document model, how SurrealDB maps tables and records to documents, and where to find guides on nested data, schema modes, and common patterns including SurrealQL and MongoDB-style mappings.
- [Schema modes](https://surrealdb.com/docs/learn/data-models/document/schema-modes): Create flexible documents without upfront column definitions, or tighten schemas with DEFINE TABLE; add and retrieve JSON-like records in SurrealQL.
- [Analyzers and tokenizers](https://surrealdb.com/docs/learn/data-models/full-text-search/analyzers-and-tokenizers): Learn how analyzers turn raw text into searchable tokens: tokenizers, filters, and testing with search::analyze before you build an index.
- [Other ways to work with text](https://surrealdb.com/docs/learn/data-models/full-text-search/other-ways-to-work-with-text): Compare and sort text with COLLATE and NUMERIC, use contains and fuzzy string metrics, regex matching, and how these complement full-text search and hybrid retrieval.
- [Full-text search model](https://surrealdb.com/docs/learn/data-models/full-text-search/overview): Learn how full-text search differs from literal matching, why SurrealDB fits FTS workloads, and where to find guides on analyzers, indexes, scoring, and non-FTS text operations.
- [Scoring and ranking](https://surrealdb.com/docs/learn/data-models/full-text-search/scoring-and-ranking): Query with the MATCHES operator, combine BM25 and HIGHLIGHTS on indexes, and use search::score and search::highlight with numbered match clauses.
- [Search indexes](https://surrealdb.com/docs/learn/data-models/full-text-search/search-indexes): Apply FULLTEXT ANALYZER indexes to single fields per index, and understand common parse errors when listing multiple columns.
- [Distance and proximity](https://surrealdb.com/docs/learn/data-models/geospatial/distance-and-proximity): Measure distance between points, reason about buffers and proximity, and use geohash helpers for hierarchical location keys alongside SurrealDB geo functions.
- [Geometry types](https://surrealdb.com/docs/learn/data-models/geospatial/geometry-types): Use GeoJSON-style geometry values in SurrealDB, including Point, LineString, Polygon, and collections, with longitude-before-latitude ordering.
- [Location-based patterns](https://surrealdb.com/docs/learn/data-models/geospatial/location-based-patterns): Apply geospatial modelling in SurrealDB to store-of-interest search, delivery zones, asset tracking, and other location-first product features.
- [Geospatial model](https://surrealdb.com/docs/learn/data-models/geospatial/overview): Learn how geospatial data differs from plain numeric fields, core ideas such as CRS and geometry types, and where to find guides on types, queries, distance, and location-based patterns.
- [Spatial queries](https://surrealdb.com/docs/learn/data-models/geospatial/spatial-queries): Combine geometry fields with SurrealQL SELECTs and geo functions to answer contains, intersects, and distance-style questions over location data.
- [Creating relations](https://surrealdb.com/docs/learn/data-models/graph/creating-relations): Create graph edges with RELATE, store data on edge tables, define TYPE RELATION for safety and tooling, and handle symmetric relations with unique indexes.
- [Graph traversal](https://surrealdb.com/docs/learn/data-models/graph/graph-traversal): Use SurrealQL arrow syntax, bidirectional edges, traversals from record IDs, automatic flattening, graph paths in schema fields, and SurrealDB Studio’s Explorer to debug paths step by step.
- [Knowledge graph patterns](https://surrealdb.com/docs/learn/data-models/graph/knowledge-graph-patterns): Model entities and relationships as first-class data for
- [Graph model](https://surrealdb.com/docs/learn/data-models/graph/overview): Learn how to think in a graph model and how SurrealDB represents nodes, edges, and properties, with links to guides on creating relations, traversal, record links, and more.
- [Record links vs graph relations](https://surrealdb.com/docs/learn/data-models/graph/record-links-vs-graph-relations): Choose between record links and graph edges for performance, schema, bidirectional references, metadata on relationships, weighting, and delete behaviour.
- [Recursive traversals](https://surrealdb.com/docs/learn/data-models/graph/recursive-traversals): Use SurrealQL recursive path syntax and idioms to walk a graph to a chosen depth and return nested structures along a relationship.
- [Social network patterns](https://surrealdb.com/docs/learn/data-models/graph/social-network-patterns): Model follows, friendships, and interaction histories with graph edges, using weighted relations and counted edges to rank “strongest” ties in a toy social graph.
- [Aggregation queries](https://surrealdb.com/docs/learn/data-models/time-series/aggregation-queries): Build downsampling with pre-computed table views, live queries, drop tables, and DEFINE EVENT for anomaly detection; compare SurrealDB to specialised TSDBs.
- [IoT and telemetry patterns](https://surrealdb.com/docs/learn/data-models/time-series/iot-and-telemetry-patterns): Model sensor readings with nested fields or complex record IDs, use range queries on array-based IDs, and attach metadata through record links.
- [Time-series model](https://surrealdb.com/docs/learn/data-models/time-series/overview): Learn how time-series workloads centre on timestamps, tags, and aggregations in SurrealDB, and where to find guides on bucketing, IoT-style modelling, and metrics.
- [Time buckets and windowing](https://surrealdb.com/docs/learn/data-models/time-series/time-buckets-and-windowing): Group time-stamped records into buckets with time::floor and GROUP BY, plan retention and downsampling, and align queries with windowed analytics workloads.
- [Using SurrealDB as a time series database](https://surrealdb.com/docs/learn/data-models/time-series/using-as-time-series-database): In this guide, you will learn how to “think” in a time-series database and show how SurrealDB helps you implement these concepts seamlessly.
- [Embedding pipelines](https://surrealdb.com/docs/learn/data-models/vector-search/embedding-pipelines): Store vector fields on records, size embeddings for throughput and accuracy, and trim dimensions when models allow.
- [Hybrid search](https://surrealdb.com/docs/learn/data-models/vector-search/hybrid-search): Compare lexical full-text search with vector similarity on the same dataset and fuse rankings with search::rrf and related helpers.
- [Vector search model](https://surrealdb.com/docs/learn/data-models/vector-search/overview): Learn how vector embeddings represent semantic similarity, how SurrealDB stores and queries vectors alongside other models, and where to find guides on pipelines, similarity, indexes, hybrid search, and RAG-style retrieval.
- [RAG architecture patterns](https://surrealdb.com/docs/learn/data-models/vector-search/rag-architecture-patterns): Map retrieval-augmented generation to SurrealDB using chunk storage, embeddings, hybrid search, filters, and operational concerns for RAG.
- [Similarity search](https://surrealdb.com/docs/learn/data-models/vector-search/similarity-search): Run SurrealQL similarity queries with the liquids example, use vector:: distance and similarity helpers, and filter KNN results with predicates.
- [Vector indexes](https://surrealdb.com/docs/learn/data-models/vector-search/vector-indexes): Choose brute force, HNSW, or DISKANN vector indexes, tune DIMENSION and distance metrics, and use the query cheat sheet with vector::distance::knn().
- [Querying](https://surrealdb.com/docs/learn/querying): Query SurrealDB with SurrealQL, SDKs or GraphQL - SQL-like syntax with graphs, links and practical querying tips.
- [Bulk operations and data import](https://surrealdb.com/docs/learn/querying/concepts-and-guides/bulk-operations-and-data-import): Bulk INSERT patterns in SurrealQL, plus Surreal Sync, HTTP import, /sql for side effects, and SurrealDB Studio CSV.
- [Connecting from serverless & edge](https://surrealdb.com/docs/learn/querying/concepts-and-guides/connecting-from-serverless-and-edge): Serverless and edge environments change how applications connect to databases.
- [Custom functions](https://surrealdb.com/docs/learn/querying/concepts-and-guides/custom-functions): Learn how to define and call database functions with fn::, optional arguments, and permissions.
- [Error handling](https://surrealdb.com/docs/learn/querying/concepts-and-guides/error-handling): Handle errors in SurrealQL with THROW, validation guards and ASSERT on fields to stop queries and return clear failures.
- [Idempotent operations](https://surrealdb.com/docs/learn/querying/concepts-and-guides/idempotent-operations): Make SurrealQL idempotent with UPSERT, safe deletes and unique indexes so retries do not corrupt data.
- [Parameterised queries](https://surrealdb.com/docs/learn/querying/concepts-and-guides/parameterised-queries): Queries can make use of parameters which hold stored values, even those from the output of a previous query.
- [Query optimisation](https://surrealdb.com/docs/learn/querying/concepts-and-guides/query-optimisation): Practical ideas for faster SurrealQL: EXPLAIN, record ranges, async events, denormalised flags, and indexes.
- [Representations and codecs](https://surrealdb.com/docs/learn/querying/concepts-and-guides/representations-and-codecs): Choose the right built-in when moving data between strings, bytes, tokens, patches, and executable query text.
- [Sequences](https://surrealdb.com/docs/learn/querying/concepts-and-guides/sequences): SurrealDB sequences for monotonic numeric identifiers, and how they differ from default randomly generated record IDs.
- [Sessions and scoping](https://surrealdb.com/docs/learn/querying/concepts-and-guides/sessions-and-scoping): A session stores information about the current connection.
- [Subqueries and advanced patterns](https://surrealdb.com/docs/learn/querying/concepts-and-guides/subqueries-and-advanced-patterns): Nested SELECTs, CREATE as a value, $parent and $this, latest record per group, and graph paths that behave like inner queries.
- [Testing](https://surrealdb.com/docs/learn/querying/concepts-and-guides/testing): This page details a number of ways that SurrealDB can be tested.
- [Transactions](https://surrealdb.com/docs/learn/querying/concepts-and-guides/transactions): How SurrealDB transactions work: the default per-statement scope, manual BEGIN, COMMIT and CANCEL, and the snapshot isolation guarantees that apply under concurrency.
- [Working with types](https://surrealdb.com/docs/learn/querying/concepts-and-guides/working-with-types): Tips for working with data types in SurrealDB, including arrays, type safety, typed LET statements, and chaining array functions.
- [Managing APIs](https://surrealdb.com/docs/learn/querying/custom-apis/managing-apis): Defining custom HTTP-style endpoints on SurrealDB so clients hit a narrow surface instead of arbitrary queries.
- [Middleware](https://surrealdb.com/docs/learn/querying/custom-apis/middleware): Chaining custom functions before your API handler so you can share logic on DEFINE API routes.
- [Mutations](https://surrealdb.com/docs/learn/querying/gql/mutations): ISO GQL data-modifying statements - INSERT, SET, REMOVE, and DELETE - on the /gql endpoint.
- [GQL](https://surrealdb.com/docs/learn/querying/gql/overview): Query SurrealDB graph data with ISO GQL - a Cypher-like graph pattern language over HTTP and RPC.
- [Sample queries](https://surrealdb.com/docs/learn/querying/gql/sample-queries): Compare common GQL graph patterns against similar SurrealQL queries on the same seed graph.
- [Via HTTP](https://surrealdb.com/docs/learn/querying/gql/via-http): Enable ISO GQL on a SurrealDB instance and run queries through POST /gql.
- [GraphQL](https://surrealdb.com/docs/learn/querying/graphql/overview): In this section, you will explore GraphQL, an industry-wide recognised protocol for interacting with your data, allowing you to query your data using any preferred method which offers precision and efficiency in data retrieval.
- [Sample queries](https://surrealdb.com/docs/learn/querying/graphql/sample-queries): Compare common GraphQL queries against similar SurrealQL SELECT patterns
- [Via Bruno](https://surrealdb.com/docs/learn/querying/graphql/via-bruno): In this section, you will explore querying SurrealDB using Bruno.
- [Via HTTP](https://surrealdb.com/docs/learn/querying/graphql/via-http): In this section, you will explore querying SurrealDB using the GraphQL HTTP endpoint. The HTTP API is designed to be simple and intuitive, with any interface that provides a consistent way to interact with the database.
- [Via SurrealDB Studio](https://surrealdb.com/docs/learn/querying/graphql/via-studio): In this section, you will explore querying SurrealDB using SurrealDB Studio.
- [Performance best practices](https://surrealdb.com/docs/learn/querying/performance/performance-best-practices): This guide outlines some key performance best practices for using SurrealDB. While SurrealDB offers powerful and flexible features to support you in meeting your desired performance standards, the use that you make of those features will ultimately determine whether or not you meet them.
- [Changefeeds](https://surrealdb.com/docs/learn/querying/real-time/changefeeds): Replaying table changes over time with changefeeds and SHOW CHANGES - useful for sync, pipelines, and external systems.
- [Live queries](https://surrealdb.com/docs/learn/querying/real-time/live-queries): Subscribing to inserts, updates, and deletes with LIVE SELECT so clients stay in sync over a persistent connection.
- [Real-time best practices](https://surrealdb.com/docs/learn/querying/real-time/real-time-best-practices): This guide outlines some best practices for using SurrealDB in an event-driven and real-time manner.
- [Executing queries](https://surrealdb.com/docs/learn/querying/surrealql/executing-queries): In this section, you will explore methods to query data in SurrealDB using SurrealQL, GraphQL or any of the available SDKs. This allows you to retrieve, filter, and manipulate data efficiently and in the best way for your use case.
- [Statements and values](https://surrealdb.com/docs/learn/querying/surrealql/statements-and-values): SurrealQL statements grouped as resource definitions, control flow with transactions, and CRUD-style query operations.
- [What is SurrealQL?](https://surrealdb.com/docs/learn/querying/surrealql/what-is-surrealql): SurrealQL is SurrealDB’s SQL-like language for queries, schemas, graph relationships and optimised execution.
- [Writing SurrealQL](https://surrealdb.com/docs/learn/querying/surrealql/writing-surrealql): Ways of executing SurrealQL queries such as SurrealDB Studio, CLI, HTTP, SDKs, and GraphQL.

- [Migrating to SurrealDB](https://surrealdb.com/docs/build/migrating): Moving data into SurrealDB from other databases, older SurrealDB releases, or files and streams.
- [Migrating](https://surrealdb.com/docs/build/migrating/from-files-and-streams): Migrating

Configure with Host URL, Port, Namespace, Database, and SurrealQL queries.

- [Distributed live queries](https://surrealdb.com/docs/manage/enterprise/capabilities/distributed-live-queries): Enterprise Edition distributed live queries across cluster nodes, and how they differ from single-node live queries.
- [Contact & licensing](https://surrealdb.com/docs/manage/enterprise/overview/contact-and-licensing): Contact SurrealDB for Enterprise Edition sales, licence models, and pricing enquiries.
- [Feature table](https://surrealdb.com/docs/manage/enterprise/overview/feature-table): Compare SurrealDB Community Edition and Enterprise Edition across security, clustering, storage, and support.
- [What EE is](https://surrealdb.com/docs/manage/enterprise/overview/what-ee-is): An overview of SurrealDB Enterprise Edition: capabilities beyond Community Edition and typical enterprise use cases.
- [Audit logging](https://surrealdb.com/docs/manage/enterprise/security/audit-logging): Enterprise Edition audit logging: captured events, log formats, storage, and SIEM integration.
- [FIPS](https://surrealdb.com/docs/manage/enterprise/security/fips): FIPS 140-2 compliance in SurrealDB Enterprise Edition: validated modules and enabling FIPS mode.
- [Trusted execution](https://surrealdb.com/docs/manage/enterprise/security/trusted-execution): Trusted execution environments (TEE) in SurrealDB Enterprise Edition: hardware requirements and attestation.
- [File storage / S3 / blob](https://surrealdb.com/docs/manage/enterprise/storage/file-storage): Enterprise Edition file and blob storage: S3-compatible backends and DEFINE BUCKET for managed file objects.
- [SLAs](https://surrealdb.com/docs/manage/enterprise/support/slas): Enterprise Edition service level agreements: uptime targets, response times by severity, and contractual support.
- [Support tiers](https://surrealdb.com/docs/manage/enterprise/support/support-tiers): SurrealDB Enterprise Edition support tiers: Standard, Premium, and Mission-Critical coverage and escalation.
- [Observability](https://surrealdb.com/docs/manage/observability): Logging, Prometheus pull, OTLP push, Enterprise pipelines, metric catalogues, and Tokio console - production visibility for SurrealDB Community and Enterprise.
- [Audit logging](https://surrealdb.com/docs/manage/observability/audit-logging): The Enterprise audit log pipeline: events captured, record shape, rotation, hash chaining, redaction and pipeline self-metrics.
- [Configuration reference](https://surrealdb.com/docs/manage/observability/configuration): Every observability, audit log and slow-query log environment variable, plus recommended configurations for local, production and multi-tenant deployments.
- [Enterprise observability](https://surrealdb.com/docs/manage/observability/enterprise-observability): Metrics, logs, and traces in SurrealDB Enterprise versus Community - OTLP opt-ins, audit and slow-query pipelines, and cluster instruments.
- [Logging](https://surrealdb.com/docs/manage/observability/logging): Server log levels, text and JSON formats, file and socket output, slow-query logging, and OpenTelemetry log levels.
- [Metrics reference](https://surrealdb.com/docs/manage/observability/metrics): Access paths, label catalogue and the complete metric reference for SurrealDB Community and Enterprise, with a migration table from 3.0.
- [Observability (metrics and Prometheus)](https://surrealdb.com/docs/manage/observability/observability): Unified OpenTelemetry metrics, `GET /metrics`, scraper authentication, naming, migration, and behaviour common to Community and Enterprise.
- [Slow-query logging](https://surrealdb.com/docs/manage/observability/slow-query-logging): The Enterprise slow-query log pipeline: how a query qualifies, record shape, rotation, hash chaining, redaction and pipeline self-metrics.
- [Telemetry (OTLP)](https://surrealdb.com/docs/manage/observability/telemetry): OTLP push export - metrics, logs, traces, intervals, backward-compatible instruments, and differences before and after SurrealDB 3.1.
- [Tokio console](https://surrealdb.com/docs/manage/observability/tokio-console): Inspect SurrealDB’s async runtime with the Tokio console - tasks, polls, and bottlenecks separate from OpenTelemetry metrics and traces.
- [Organisations](https://surrealdb.com/docs/manage/organisations): The container for instances, members, usage, and billing, and what each section of the organisation view holds.
- [AWS Marketplace](https://surrealdb.com/docs/manage/organisations/aws-marketplace): Subscribe through AWS Marketplace so charges appear on your AWS bill, and link the subscription to an organisation.
- [Billing](https://surrealdb.com/docs/manage/organisations/billing): Organisation-level billing details, payment methods, discount codes, invoices, and the usage that produces them.
- [FAQs](https://surrealdb.com/docs/manage/organisations/faqs): Common questions about managed instances: getting started, limits, security, pricing, legal terms, and troubleshooting.
- [Members and roles](https://surrealdb.com/docs/manage/organisations/members-and-roles): Invite people to an organisation, track pending invitations, and choose between the Owner, Admin, and Member roles.
- [Referrals](https://surrealdb.com/docs/manage/organisations/referrals): Share a referral link to earn credits and rewards when someone signs up through it.
- [Accounts and sign-in](https://surrealdb.com/docs/manage/organisations/sign-in): Create an account with Google, GitHub, email, or a passkey, and sign in to manage organisations and instances.
- [Support](https://surrealdb.com/docs/manage/organisations/support): Community help, paid support plans, raising a ticket, and what Surreal Sidekick can answer.
- [SurrealKit schema migration](https://surrealdb.com/docs/manage/schema-migration): SurrealKit is the official schema management and migration CLI for SurrealDB. Define your schema in .surql files and keep databases in sync across every environment.
- [embed_schema! macro](https://surrealdb.com/docs/manage/schema-migration/embed-schema-macro): The embed_schema! macro bakes your .surql schema files into the Rust binary at compile time, so schema is always in sync with the application that ships it.
- [Using SurrealKit as a library](https://surrealdb.com/docs/manage/schema-migration/library): Embed SurrealKit directly in a Rust application to connect to SurrealDB, sync schema at startup, run rollouts, and seed data without the CLI.
- [Rollouts](https://surrealdb.com/docs/manage/schema-migration/rollouts): Rollouts provide a controlled, phased migration workflow for shared and production SurrealDB databases, with review, staged execution, and rollback support.
- [Sync](https://surrealdb.com/docs/manage/schema-migration/sync): Sync pushes your .surql schema files to SurrealDB immediately, keeping the database in desired state. Use it for local development and ephemeral environments.
- [Template variables](https://surrealdb.com/docs/manage/schema-migration/template-variables): Template variables let you parameterise .surql schema files with environment-specific values, substituted at runtime by SurrealKit.
- [Project templates](https://surrealdb.com/docs/manage/schema-migration/templates): surrealkit init scaffolds a project from a template with selectable features. Use the bundled template, pick only the features you need, or supply your own.
- [Testing](https://surrealdb.com/docs/manage/schema-migration/testing): SurrealKit includes a built-in testing framework for validating schema correctness, permissions, and API behaviour across multiple actor types.
- [Type generation](https://surrealdb.com/docs/manage/schema-migration/typegen): surrealkit typegen introspects a live database and emits a structured JSON schema document, with optional TypeScript types for the SurrealDB JavaScript SDK.
- [Existing databases](https://surrealdb.com/docs/manage/schema-migration/getting-started/existing-databases): Adopt SurrealKit in a project that already has a SurrealDB database by capturing a baseline snapshot and moving to the Rollouts workflow.
- [New databases](https://surrealdb.com/docs/manage/schema-migration/getting-started/new-databases): Start a new SurrealDB project with SurrealKit from the beginning, writing schema files and syncing to a local database.
- [Sync vs Rollouts](https://surrealdb.com/docs/manage/schema-migration/getting-started/sync-vs-rollouts): Understand when to use SurrealKit's Sync mode for development and Rollouts mode for production, and how teams typically combine both.
- [Library usage example](https://surrealdb.com/docs/manage/schema-migration/library/example): Worked examples of using SurrealKit's library API for both sync and rollouts in a Rust application.
- [CI / CD](https://surrealdb.com/docs/manage/schema-migration/testing/ci-cd): Run SurrealKit tests in CI pipelines using the official GitHub Action, with JSON output for test reporting and Docker Compose for full end-to-end environments.
- [Instances](https://surrealdb.com/docs/manage/instances): What an instance is, how the Start and Scale plans differ, and where each operational task is documented.
- [Architecture](https://surrealdb.com/docs/manage/instances/architecture): The single-node and multi-node topologies behind the Start and Scale plans, and what each one means for growth and recovery.
- [Backups and recovery](https://surrealdb.com/docs/manage/instances/backups): Automated snapshots, retention tiers, and restoring a snapshot into a new instance.
- [Configure an instance](https://surrealdb.com/docs/manage/instances/configure): Instance settings in SurrealDB Studio: capabilities, compute and storage, pausing, and deletion.
- [Connect to an instance](https://surrealdb.com/docs/manage/instances/connect): The four routes to an instance: SurrealDB Studio, the CLI, a client SDK, and the HTTP API. Includes where to find the connection details.
- [Create an instance](https://surrealdb.com/docs/manage/instances/create): Deploy an instance from SurrealDB Studio: choose a plan, instance type, region, version, name, starting data, and storage.
- [High availability](https://surrealdb.com/docs/manage/instances/high-availability): What a Start instance and a Scale cluster each survive, and how to plan for the failures they do not.
- [Import and export](https://surrealdb.com/docs/manage/instances/import-and-export): Move data in and out of an instance with surreal export and surreal import, including size limits and partial-import behaviour.
- [Monitoring](https://surrealdb.com/docs/manage/instances/monitoring): The instance dashboard, the metrics groups and log filters in SurrealDB Studio, and how they relate to the full observability surface.
- [Network access](https://surrealdb.com/docs/manage/instances/network-access): Control which outbound destinations queries may reach, using the network access capability and its allow and deny patterns.
- [Private connectivity](https://surrealdb.com/docs/manage/instances/private-connectivity): Reach an instance from your AWS VPC over AWS PrivateLink, and set the public, private, or dual access mode.
- [Scaling](https://surrealdb.com/docs/manage/instances/scaling): When to resize an instance, what scales on each plan, and how to confirm a resize solved the bottleneck.
- [Versions and upgrades](https://surrealdb.com/docs/manage/instances/versions-and-upgrades): Change the SurrealDB release an instance runs, and what happens to the instance during the upgrade.
- [Via CLI](https://surrealdb.com/docs/manage/instances/connect/via-cli): Open an interactive SurrealQL shell against an instance with surreal sql, and where to get the token.
- [Via HTTP](https://surrealdb.com/docs/manage/instances/connect/via-http): Query an instance with cURL or any HTTP client, and the request size limits that apply per endpoint.
- [Via SDK](https://surrealdb.com/docs/manage/instances/connect/via-sdk): Connect to an instance from application code, including the credentials each SDK needs and how to create them.
- [Via SurrealDB Studio](https://surrealdb.com/docs/manage/instances/connect/via-studio): Select a namespace and database, then query an instance from the SurrealDB Studio query view.
- [surrealctl](https://surrealdb.com/docs/manage/surrealctl): The control-plane CLI: what surrealctl does, when to reach for it instead of SurrealDB Studio or the surreal binary, and a sixty-second quickstart.
- [Authentication](https://surrealdb.com/docs/manage/surrealctl/authentication): Choose between a login session and a personal access token, store credentials safely, and authenticate an unattended run.
- [Install](https://surrealdb.com/docs/manage/surrealctl/install): Install surrealctl on macOS, Linux, or Windows, verify the download, sign in for the first time, and keep the binary up to date.
- [Instances](https://surrealdb.com/docs/manage/surrealctl/instances): Deploy, find, connect to, scale, pause, back up, and delete instances with the surrealctl instance commands.
- [Organisations](https://surrealdb.com/docs/manage/surrealctl/organisations): Select an organisation, manage members and invitations, check roles, and read usage and spend from the command line.
- [Scripting](https://surrealdb.com/docs/manage/surrealctl/scripting): Drive surrealctl from CI and shell scripts: the JSON contract, exit codes for control flow, unattended runs, and waiting semantics.
- [Self-hosted](https://surrealdb.com/docs/manage/self-hosted): Deploy and operate SurrealDB on your own infrastructure: deployment models, containers, configuration, backups, monitoring, and upgrades.
- [Backups & recovery](https://surrealdb.com/docs/manage/self-hosted/backups-and-recovery): Create and restore SurrealQL backups with the CLI, plan backup strategies, and prepare for disaster recovery.
- [Configuration](https://surrealdb.com/docs/manage/self-hosted/configuration): Configure a self-hosted SurrealDB server: CLI options, environment variables, storage, networking, auth, and TLS.
- [Deployment models](https://surrealdb.com/docs/manage/self-hosted/deployment-models): Deployment models for SurrealDB - managed instances, single-node RocksDB, multi-node clusters, and embedded runtimes - and how to choose between them.
- [Docker](https://surrealdb.com/docs/manage/self-hosted/docker): A tutorial to run SurrealDB from within Docker.
- [Kubernetes](https://surrealdb.com/docs/manage/self-hosted/kubernetes): Deploy SurrealDB to Kubernetes with RocksDB on a persistent volume.
- [Managed Kubernetes](https://surrealdb.com/docs/manage/self-hosted/managed-kubernetes): Options for running SurrealDB on Amazon EKS, Google GKE, and Azure AKS - managed Scale, self-hosted Enterprise clusters, or single-node RocksDB.
- [Monitoring & observability](https://surrealdb.com/docs/manage/self-hosted/monitoring-and-observability): Health checks, OpenTelemetry metrics and traces, audit logs and slow-query logs, and integration with common observability stacks.
- [Upgrades & patching](https://surrealdb.com/docs/manage/self-hosted/upgrades-and-patching): Upgrade SurrealDB safely: binary replacement, surreal fix for major versions, migrations, and cluster rolling upgrades.

- [Query SurrealDB from Postman](https://surrealdb.com/docs/explore/tutorials/tutorials/http-via-postman): In this tutorial, you will learn how to query the SurrealDB RESTful HTTP API endpoints using Postman.
- [Build a minimal LangChain chatbot](https://surrealdb.com/docs/explore/tutorials/tutorials/minimal-langchain): This tutorial shows how to build a minimal LangChain chatbot with both vector and graph.
- [Tutorials](https://surrealdb.com/docs/explore/tutorials/tutorials/overview): Step-by-step tutorials and walkthroughs for specific tasks with SurrealDB: integrations, real-time apps, AI patterns, and more.
- [Implement semantic search in Rust](https://surrealdb.com/docs/explore/tutorials/tutorials/semantic-search-in-rust): In this guide, you'll learn how to implement semantic search in Rust using either Mistral AI or OpenAI via their Rust crates.

## Reference

- [Python SDK](https://surrealdb.com/docs/reference/python): The SurrealDB SDK for Python enables simple and advanced querying of a remote or embedded database.
- [Installation](https://surrealdb.com/docs/reference/python/installation): In this section, you will learn how to install the Python SDK in your project.
- [Go SDK](https://surrealdb.com/docs/reference/golang): The SurrealDB SDK for Go enables simple and advanced querying of a remote database from server-side applications.
- [Embedding](https://surrealdb.com/docs/reference/golang/embedding): The surrealdb.c C FFI library contains Go bindings that can be used to access an embedded SurrealDB instance.
- [Installation](https://surrealdb.com/docs/reference/golang/installation): The SurrealDB Go SDK can be installed with a single go get command.
- [Rust SDK](https://surrealdb.com/docs/reference/rust): The SurrealDB SDK for Rust enables you to interact with SurrealDB from client-side, server-side applications, systems, APIs, embedded systems, and IoT devices.
- [SDK Concepts](https://surrealdb.com/docs/reference/rust/concepts): The SurrealDB SDK for Rust enables simple and advanced querying of a remote or embedded database.
- [Embedding](https://surrealdb.com/docs/reference/rust/embedding): In Rust, SurrealDB can be run as an in-memory database, it can persist data using a file-based storage engine, or on a distributed cluster.
- [Crates](https://surrealdb.com/docs/reference/rust/frameworks): The following pages each contain a tutorial that walks through the setting up of a web server (for Actix, Axum, and Rocket) or a UI (for Egui) that uses SurrealDB as its storage backend.
- [SDK methods](https://surrealdb.com/docs/reference/rust/methods): Most methods in the SurrealDB SDK involve either working with or creating an instance of the Surreal struct, which serves as the database client instance for embedded or remote databases.
- [Java SDK](https://surrealdb.com/docs/reference/java): The SurrealDB SDK for Java enables simple and advanced querying of a remote or embedded database.
- [Installation](https://surrealdb.com/docs/reference/java/installation): The SurrealDB SDK for Java is available on Maven Central and can be installed using Gradle or Maven.
- [Kotlin SDK](https://surrealdb.com/docs/reference/kotlin): The SurrealDB SDK for Kotlin is a coroutine-based, Kotlin Multiplatform client for querying a remote SurrealDB instance.
- [Installation](https://surrealdb.com/docs/reference/kotlin/installation): The SurrealDB SDK for Kotlin is published to Maven Central and can be installed using Gradle or Maven.
- [CLI Tools](https://surrealdb.com/docs/reference/cli): Reference for the three SurrealDB command-line tools: surrealctl for the control plane, surreal for the data plane, and surqlfmt for formatting SurrealQL.
- [PHP SDK](https://surrealdb.com/docs/reference/php): The SurrealDB SDK for PHP lets you query a remote SurrealDB instance from any PHP application, with a stable v1 release and a v2 rewrite in alpha.
- [PHP SDK v1](https://surrealdb.com/docs/reference/php/v1): Version 1 is the current stable release of the SurrealDB PHP SDK, with direct RPC-style methods for querying a remote database.
- [PHP SDK v2](https://surrealdb.com/docs/reference/php/v2): Version 2 of the SurrealDB SDK for PHP is a rewrite with a fluent query builder, typed credentials, and a PSR-based transport layer.
- [.NET SDK](https://surrealdb.com/docs/reference/dotnet): The SurrealDB SDK for .NET provides a number of methods for interacting with your SurrealDB database.
- [SDK concepts](https://surrealdb.com/docs/reference/dotnet/core): The .NET SDK for SurrealDB enables simple and advanced querying of a remote or embedded database.
- [Data types](https://surrealdb.com/docs/reference/dotnet/data-types): The .NET SDK translates all datatypes native to SurrealQL into either datatypes native to .NET, or a custom implementation. This document describes all datatypes, and links to their respective documentation.
- [Embedding](https://surrealdb.com/docs/reference/dotnet/embedding): The documentation for embedding SurrealDB within .NET.
- [Installation](https://surrealdb.com/docs/reference/dotnet/installation): In this section, you will learn how to install the .NET SDK in your project.
- [SDK methods](https://surrealdb.com/docs/reference/dotnet/methods): The .NET SDK for SurrealDB has a single SurrealDB class that provides methods for querying a remote SurrealDB database.
- [SurrealQL](https://surrealdb.com/docs/reference/query-language): Reference for SurrealQL, SurrealDB's query language: statements, clauses, functions, and language primitives.
- [Swift SDK](https://surrealdb.com/docs/reference/swift): The SurrealDB SDK for Swift enables simple and advanced querying of a remote database from Apple-platform and server-side Swift applications.
- [Data types](https://surrealdb.com/docs/reference/swift/data-types): An overview of the data types used by the SurrealDB Swift SDK, including SurrealValue and SurrealRecordID.
- [Installation](https://surrealdb.com/docs/reference/swift/installation): In this section, you will learn how to install the Swift SDK in your project.
- [SDK methods](https://surrealdb.com/docs/reference/swift/methods): The Swift SDK for SurrealDB enables simple and advanced querying of a remote database.
- [Mojo SDK](https://surrealdb.com/docs/reference/mojo): The SurrealDB SDK for Mojo enables simple and advanced querying of a remote database over HTTP, HTTPS, and WebSocket.
- [Installation](https://surrealdb.com/docs/reference/mojo/installation): In this section, you will learn how to install the SurrealDB Mojo SDK and add it to your project.
- [SDK methods](https://surrealdb.com/docs/reference/mojo/methods): The full method reference for the SurrealDB Mojo SDK.
- [JavaScript SDK](https://surrealdb.com/docs/reference/javascript): The SurrealDB SDK for JavaScript enables simple and advanced querying of a remote or embedded database.
- [API reference](https://surrealdb.com/docs/reference/javascript/api): Complete reference for the JavaScript SDK's classes, query builders, data types, and errors.
- [Installation](https://surrealdb.com/docs/reference/javascript/installation): In this section, you will learn how to install the JavaScript SDK in your project.
- [REST API](https://surrealdb.com/docs/reference/rest-api): SurrealDB exposes an HTTP-based REST API for executing queries, managing authentication, and performing CRUD operations.
- [CBOR protocol](https://surrealdb.com/docs/reference/rest-api/cbor-protocol): SurrealDB supports a number of methods for connecting to the database and performing data queries.
- [HTTP protocol](https://surrealdb.com/docs/reference/rest-api/http-protocol): The HTTP endpoints enable selection and modification of data, along with custom SurrealQL queries, using traditional RESTful HTTP endpoints.
- [Postgres wire protocol](https://surrealdb.com/docs/reference/rest-api/postgres-protocol): Connect to SurrealDB with standard Postgres clients and drivers, run SurrealQL or ISO GQL, and receive tabular typed results over the Postgres v3 wire protocol.
- [RPC protocol](https://surrealdb.com/docs/reference/rest-api/rpc-protocol): The RPC protocol allows for easy bidirectional communication with SurrealDB.
